name: Disk Forensics — Autopsy, MFTECmd, EvtxECmd, Registry, Timeline Explorer & EQL
command: chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe hunt .\kapefiles\auto\C%3A\Windows\System32\winevt\Logs -s sigma/ --mapping mappings/sigma-event-logs-all.yml -r rules/ --csv --output output_csv
description: Disk forensics tools for Windows incident response. Autopsy: GUI case management; Data Sources, Web Artifacts, Keyword Search, Timeline Analysis, Deleted File Recovery, OS Accounts, SRUM/Run Programs, ADS/Zone.Identifier viewing. MFTECmd: parse $MFT, $J, MFT Explorer GUI for deleted file recovery. EvtxECmd: parse EVTX to CSV with event maps; load into Timeline Explorer. EQL (Endgame Event Query Language): pip install eql; query Sysmon JSON for process creation chains. Registry Explorer: GUI for hive files; bookmarks for ShimCache, BAM, Run keys. RegRipper: rip.exe -r <hive> -p <plugin>; key plugins: compname, timezone, nic2, installer, recentdocs, run, bam. Timeline Explorer: drag-and-drop CSV from MFTECmd/PECmd/EvtxECmd; chronological correlation. Chainsaw: hunt EVTX with Sigma rules; outputs account_tampering.csv, antivirus.csv, sigma.csv. pagefile.sys: keyword search in Autopsy recovers deleted file content.
source: CDSA Module 13: Introduction to Digital Forensics
notes:
=== ERIC ZIMMERMAN TOOLS ===
Download all: Get-ZimmermanTools.ps1
  → Installs to C:\Users\johndoe\Desktop\Get-ZimmermanTools\net6\

Key tools:
  MFTECmd.exe          → Parse $MFT, $J (USN Journal), $Boot, $SDS
  MFTExplorer           → GUI for browsing $MFT
  PECmd.exe            → Parse prefetch files
  AppCompatCacheParser.exe  → Parse ShimCache from SYSTEM hive
  AmcacheParser.exe    → Parse Amcache.hve
  ShellBagsExplorer    → GUI for shellbags
  EvtxECmd.exe         → Parse EVTX event logs with maps
  LECmd.exe            → Parse LNK files
  Timeline Explorer    → GUI for loading/correlating CSV outputs
  Registry Explorer    → GUI for hive files with bookmarks
  JLECmd.exe           → Parse Jump Lists

=== MFTECMD — MFT AND USN JOURNAL ===

Parse $MFT:
  MFTECmd.exe -f C:\evidence\$MFT --csv C:\output --csvf mft.csv

Parse USN Journal ($J):
  MFTECmd.exe -f C:\kapefiles\$Extend\$J --csv C:\output --csvf MFT-J.csv

Dump single MFT entry (shows $SI and $FN timestamps — detect timestomping):
  MFTECmd.exe -f $MFT --de <entry_hex_value>
  → Both $STANDARD_INFORMATION and $FILE_NAME timestamps shown
  → SI modifiable by user-space tools; FN only by kernel → discrepancy = timestomping

Search for deleted file in $MFT CSV:
  Select-String -Path mft_csv.csv -Pattern "flag.txt"
  → Returns: path, timestamps, InUse=False → file is deleted (entry marked free)

MFT Explorer GUI:
  Open Amcache.hve-style: File → Load → select $MFT file
  Deleted files marked with 'Is deleted' attribute in right pane
  Resident data: small files stored directly in MFT record

=== PECMD — PREFETCH ANALYSIS ===

Single file:
  PECmd.exe -f RUNDLL32.EXE-F11DC80E.pf
  → Shows: run count, last run, first run, other runs, files loaded, dirs referenced
  → Look for: Zone.Identifier ADS entries in files list

Directory (all prefetch files) to CSV:
  PECmd.exe -d C:\Windows\Prefetch --csv C:\output --csvf prefetch.csv
  → Creates: prefetch.csv (per-file details) + prefetch_Timeline.csv (sorted by run time)

Quiet mode + CSV (used in lab):
  PECmd.exe -d "kapefiles\auto\C%3A\Windows\Prefetch" -q --csv C:\Desktop --csvf suspect_prefetch.csv

Load both CSVs into Timeline Explorer for chronological view.
Suspicious in prefetch: executables running from %TEMP%, Downloads, Tasks, or unusual paths

=== EVTXECMD — EVENT LOG PARSING ===

Basic parse:
  EvtxECmd.exe -f Security.evtx --csv C:\output --csvf security.csv

Parse with maps (converts EventData fields to named columns):
  EvtxECmd.exe -f Security.evtx --csv C:\output --csvf security.csv
  → Maps live in: EvtxECmd\Maps\
  → Maps convert raw XML EventData into: UserName, ExecutableInfo, PayloadData1-6, RemoteHost

Sync maps from GitHub (get latest):
  EvtxECmd.exe --sync

Filter specific EventIDs:
  EvtxECmd.exe -f Security.evtx --csv C:\output --inc 4624,4625,4688

Parse entire directory of EVTX:
  EvtxECmd.exe -d C:\evtx_dir --csv C:\output --csvf all_events.csv

Load output CSV into Timeline Explorer → filter by TimeCreated, EventId, PayloadData

Key Event IDs:
  4624 = Logon success      4625 = Logon failure
  4688 = Process creation   4689 = Process termination
  4720 = User account created
  4732 = Member added to security-enabled local group (Administrators)
  4776 = NTLM authentication
  7045 = New service installed
  1 (Sysmon) = Process creation   10 = Process access
  3 (Sysmon) = Network connection

=== TIMELINE EXPLORER ===
GUI tool; drag-and-drop CSV files from:
  PECmd.exe output (prefetch_Timeline.csv)
  MFTECmd.exe output (MFT-J.csv)
  EvtxECmd.exe output (events.csv)

Features:
  → Chronological event view across all sources
  → Filter/search by date range, keyword, column value
  → Color-code rows
  → Pin/bookmark important events

Workflow: load PECmd_Timeline.csv + EvtxECmd.csv → filter to incident time window
→ Correlate prefetch execution times with event log activity

=== EQL (ENDGAME EVENT QUERY LANGUAGE) ===
Pip install: pip install eql

Setup — convert Sysmon EVTX to EQL-queryable JSON:
  Import-Module .\scrape-events.ps1
  $events = Get-EventProps -Path C:\events\Sysmon.evtx
  $events | ConvertTo-Json | Out-File events.json

Query syntax:
  eql query -f events.json "<query>"

Example — find net.exe reconnaissance:
  eql query -f events.json "EventId=1 and (Image='*net.exe' and (wildcard(CommandLine, '* user*', '*localgroup *', '*group *')))"

Example — process creation by parent:
  eql query -f events.json "sequence [process where Image='*cmd.exe'] [process where Image='*powershell.exe']"

EventId=1 = Sysmon process creation
Wildcard patterns: use * for any characters; case-insensitive by default
sequence: find events in order across time

=== REGISTRY EXPLORER ===
GUI tool; open hive files directly (no installation into live registry).

Hive files to load:
  SYSTEM      → ShimCache, timezone, services
  SOFTWARE    → installed software, Run keys, version info
  NTUSER.DAT  → per-user Run keys, UserAssist, MRUs, BAM
  SECURITY    → LSA secrets
  SAM         → user accounts

Bookmarks (pre-mapped locations):
  AppCompatCache  → ShimCache: full path + timestamps + execution flag
  bam             → Background Activity Moderator: last exec time per user
  CurrentVersion  → Run/RunOnce autostart keys
  UserAssist      → GUI app launch history
  RecentDocs      → recently opened files
  TypedURLs       → URLs typed in IE/Edge

Drag-and-drop hive file → navigate with bookmarks → right-click → export

=== REGRIPPER ===
Command-line registry plugin parser.

Basic syntax:
  rip.exe -r <hive_file> -p <plugin_name>

Key plugins:
  compname    → Computer name (SYSTEM hive)
  timezone    → System timezone (SYSTEM hive)
  nic2        → Network adapters, IP addresses, MAC (SYSTEM hive)
  installer   → Installed software (SOFTWARE hive)
  recentdocs  → Recently accessed documents (NTUSER.DAT)
  run         → HKCU/HKLM Run autostart keys (NTUSER.DAT or SOFTWARE)
  bam         → BAM execution timestamps (SYSTEM hive)
  userassist  → UserAssist (NTUSER.DAT)

List ALL plugins (export to CSV):
  rip.exe -l -c > rip_plugins.csv

Examples:
  rip.exe -r SYSTEM -p compname         → computer name
  rip.exe -r SYSTEM -p timezone         → timezone
  rip.exe -r SYSTEM -p nic2             → network adapters / IPs
  rip.exe -r SOFTWARE -p installer      → installed programs
  rip.exe -r NTUSER.DAT -p recentdocs   → recent files
  rip.exe -r NTUSER.DAT -p run          → user Run key entries
  rip.exe -r SYSTEM -p bam              → BAM execution times

=== AUTOPSY ===
GUI digital forensics case manager.

Add evidence:
  File → New Case → Add Data Source → Disk Image (.E01/.raw), Local Disk, or folder

Key views:
  Data Sources    → browse file system tree; view ADS (Zone.Identifier)
  Web Artifacts   → Web Downloads (source URL, referrer, timestamps)
  OS Accounts     → user account creation times
  Data Artifacts → Run Programs (SRUM/SRUDB.dat), Installed Programs
  Keyword Search  → search for strings across all artifacts
  Timeline Analysis → chronological view (uses Plaso behind the scenes)

Timestomping detection in Autopsy:
  Navigate to file → File Metadata tab
  Compare:
    $FILE_NAME MFT Modified     = kernel-written = real creation/mod time
    $STANDARD_INFORMATION File Modified = user-space writable = potentially stomped
  Discrepancy = timestomping (T1070.006)

Deleted file recovery:
  Deleted files have 'Is deleted' badge in file listing
  Right-click → Extract File(s)
  File may be partially in pagefile.sys if overwritten

pagefile.sys recovery:
  Keyword Search → search partial known content → pagefile.sys hit → view content
  Even overwritten files may have fragments in pagefile (Windows RAM overflow)

ISO/ADS workflow in Autopsy:
  Downloads folder → .Zone.Identifier stream → HostUrl = download source
  Web Downloads artifact confirms the same URL
  ISO → extract → mount → contains DLL + LNK → LNK runs rundll32.exe payload.dll,StartW

=== CHAINSAW — SIGMA HUNTING ON EVTX ===

Hunt with Sigma rules + built-in rules:
  chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe hunt <evtx_path> \
    -s sigma/ --mapping mappings/sigma-event-logs-all.yml \
    -r rules/ --csv --output output_csv

Output files in output_csv/:
  sigma.csv           → all Sigma rule detections
  account_tampering.csv  → user creation / group membership changes
  antivirus.csv       → AV detections

Lab results from sigma.csv:
  → Cobalt Strike Load by rundll32
  → Cobalt Strike Named Pipe (post-exploitation covert comms)
  → UAC Bypass via fodhelper.exe (T1548.002)
  → LSASS Access (Mimikatz / credential dumping)
  → Windows PowerShell base64 execution

From account_tampering.csv:
  → New user 'Admin' created + added to Administrators group

KEY GOTCHA: mapping file must contain all fields referenced by Sigma rules.
  sigma-event-logs-all.yml may miss fields like NewProcessName (EID 4688)
  → Use sigma-event-logs-all-new.yml (extended) or add missing field mappings

=== FULL INVESTIGATION WORKFLOW ===
1. Collect: KAPE !SANS_Triage + WinPmem (PhysicalMemory.raw)
2. Memory analysis: Volatility pslist/pstree/malfind/cmdline/netstat/dlllist → identify PID
3. Disk artifacts:
   a. MFTECmd $MFT → timeline of file creation
   b. MFTECmd $J → file operations (STREAM_CHANGE on .iso = MotW written)
   c. Autopsy → keyword search "payload.dll" → find Finance08062023.iso in Downloads
   d. Web Downloads artifact → HostUrl = letsgohunt[.]site
   e. PECmd prefetch → RUNDLL32.EXE-*.pf → first/last run times
   f. EvtxECmd → parse Security + Sysmon → load in Timeline Explorer
   g. Chainsaw → Sigma hunt → detect CS named pipe, UAC bypass, LSASS access
   h. Registry Explorer / RegRipper → Run keys → C:\ProgramData\svchost.exe persistence
   i. Autoruns (.arn) → Logon + Scheduled Tasks → malicious entries
   j. SRUM in Autopsy → bytes exfiltrated per process
4. Correlate all timestamps in Timeline Explorer
5. Reconstruct attack timeline for report
